statement: LEMMA. For nu>=lambda, nu>=mu: there exists a pair {a,b} subset nu with nu\{a,b} >= lambda and nu\{a,b} >= mu  <=>  |nu| - max(|lambda|,|mu|) >= 2. Forward by cardinality; backward by deleting the two SMALLEST elements of nu, which leaves the top max(|lambda|,|mu|) elements untouched because Motegi's order compares only the top r. This is WHERE THE max COMES FROM: a pole needs the deleted pair to dominate BOTH lambda and mu, an 'and' whose negation is the 'or' that makes the criterion read min(|nu|-|lambda|,|nu|-|mu|)<=1.
approach: Pure combinatorics on Motegi's shifted-dominance order: forward by cardinality, backward by deleting the two SMALLEST elements of nu, which leaves the compared top-r window untouched.

Motegi's order MLe is defined in his own INCREASING enumeration (arXiv:2610.15344 Thm 2.6(i)); the 'top r elements' reading is the theorem MLe_iff_desc, proved against an independently constructed decreasing enumeration, so the definition is checked against a different characterisation than the one it was coded from. Key lemma asc_erase_two: in the ascending convention, deleting the two smallest elements is a cons-strip at the FRONT, closed by rfl. SURVIVING LESION: (a)=>(b) needs NEITHER order hypothesis -- now lem_comb_forward, a free strengthening of the tex statement.
